# New-ZbxGraph

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a graph.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxGraph [[-Name] <string>] [-Uuid <string>] [-YMinItemId <ulong>] [-YMaxItemId <ulong>] [-GraphItem <ZabbixGraphItemRequest[]>] [-Width <int>] [-Height <int>] [-YAxisMin <double>] [-YAxisMax <double>] [-ShowWorkPeriod <bool>] [-ShowTriggers <bool>] [-GraphType <ZabbixGraphType>] [-ShowLegend <bool>] [-Show3d <bool>] [-PercentLeft <double>] [-PercentRight <double>] [-YMinType <ZabbixGraphYAxisType>] [-YMaxType <ZabbixGraphYAxisType>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A graph plots the values of one or more items over time, as lines, stacked areas, a pie or an exploded pie. The New-ZbxGraph cmdlet sends graph.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new graph back with graph.get and writes it. The server requires -Name and -GraphItem; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create a graph

```powershell
$item = Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' -Name 'CPU utilization'
New-ZbxGraph -Name 'CPU load' -GraphItem @{ itemid = $item.ItemId; color = '1A7C11' } -Width 900 -Height 200
```

Creates a graph named CPU load. The command writes the new graph, read back from the server.
